title: Intrinsic and extrinsic connectivity of the seizure onset zone at rest and during stimulation
title_zh: 静息与刺激状态下癫痫发作起始区的内在与外在连接性
abstract: BACKGROUND: About half of patients who undergo epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant epilepsy have seizure recurrence, supporting the need for approaches that more accurately identify the epileptogenic zone, defined as the brain areas whose removal causes cessation of seizures. Altered network connectivity has emerged as a candidate biomarker of the epileptogenic zone, but how connectivity is altered in the epileptogenic zone remains uncertain, with prior studies reporting inconsistent results. HYPOTHESIS: We hypothesized that a difference in intrinsic versus extrinsic connectivity of the epileptogenic zone may explain prior discrepant findings. METHODS: We retrospectively studied a multicenter cohort of 37 adult and 42 pediatric patients who underwent intracranial EEG recording and brain stimulation as part of epilepsy surgery planning. We measured spontaneous connectivity using Pearson correlation and perturbational connectivity using stimulation evoked potentials, modeling the connectivity according to the location of contacts in relation to the seizure onset zone while controlling for inter-electrode distance. RESULTS: For both adult and pediatric patients, resting connectivity was higher within compared to outside the seizure onset zone. However, resting connectivity between channels within and outside seizure onset zone was reduced. Stimulation connectivity followed a similar pattern, with elevated connectivity within the seizure onset zone but reduced connectivity from within to outside seizure onset zone. SIGNIFICANCE: These results support the hypothesis that the seizure onset zone is disconnected from the rest of the brain but intrinsically hyperconnected. This result helps reconcile prior inconsistencies across studies, aligns with basic science studies, and suggests an approach for future translational work aiming to localize the epileptogenic zone.
abstract_zh: 背景：约一半接受药物难治性癫痫手术的患者会出现癫痫复发，这表明需要更准确识别癫痫发作区（即切除后可停止癫痫发作的脑区）的手段。网络连接性改变已成为癫痫发作区的潜在生物标志，但该区的连接性如何改变仍不确定，先前研究结果不一致。假设：我们假设癫痫发作区的内在与外在连接性差异可能解释先前的矛盾发现。方法：我们回顾性研究了37名成人和42名儿童多中心队列，这些患者在癫痫手术规划中接受了颅内电生理记录和脑刺激。我们使用Pearson相关系数测量自发连接性，使用刺激诱发电位测量扰动连接性，并根据电极接触点相对于癫痫发作起始区的位置建模连接性，同时控制电极间距。结果：在成人和儿童患者中，静息状态下，发作起始区内的连接性高于区外。然而，发作起始区内外通道之间的静息连接性降低。刺激连接性呈类似模式，在发作起始区内连接性升高，但从区内到区外的连接性降低。意义：这些结果支持癫痫发作起始区与大脑其余部分断联但内部超连接的假设。该结果有助于调和先前研究的不一致，符合基础科学研究，并为未来旨在定位癫痫发作区的转化工作提供了方法。
